This document is a comprehensive set of course notes on differential equations, prepared specifically for students in the final year of secondary school who are preparing for national examinations. It represents the culmination of several years of teaching experience and has been refined through classroom feedback from multiple cohorts of students with different learning styles and academic backgrounds.

The material begins with a thorough review of the foundational concepts that underpin the entire theory. Single-variable calculus, differentiation rules, integration techniques, and elementary algebra are revisited briefly to ensure that every reader has the necessary mathematical maturity before progressing to more advanced topics. This preliminary chapter is deliberately concise but complete enough to serve as a reliable reference throughout the rest of the document.

The first substantial chapter introduces ordinary differential equations and explains their fundamental role in modeling physical phenomena. Readers encounter the distinction between equations of different orders, the meaning of a solution, and the conditions under which solutions exist and are unique. Separable equations are treated first because they offer the most accessible entry point into the subject. Worked examples demonstrate each transformation step by step, and the reasoning behind every algebraic manipulation is made explicit rather than assumed.

Linear equations with constant coefficients form the subject of the second chapter. The method of integrating factors is developed gradually, starting from the simplest cases and building toward more general formulations. Special attention is devoted to understanding why the method works, not merely how to apply it. Several exercises encourage readers to verify intermediate steps independently, reinforcing both confidence and competence.

The third chapter extends the discussion to second-order equations. The method of undetermined coefficients is presented alongside the more general technique of variation of parameters. Comparison between the two approaches helps readers appreciate the trade-offs between convenience and generality. Applications to mechanical oscillations, electrical circuits, and simple population models appear throughout, grounding abstract techniques in concrete scenarios that motivate sustained engagement.

A distinctive feature of this document is the systematic use of diagrams. Slope fields, solution curves, and phase portraits are illustrated with clear captions and detailed annotations. Geometric interpretations complement the analytic treatment, helping readers develop intuition that persists beyond the formal manipulation of symbols. The visual language is consistent across chapters, reducing cognitive load and facilitating efficient revision.

Review questions conclude every section. They range from routine verification exercises to open-ended problems requiring genuine mathematical reasoning. Full solutions are provided, but the emphasis is always on the reasoning process rather than on the final numerical answer. Common misconceptions are addressed directly, and readers are encouraged to reflect on why certain errors are tempting before understanding why they are incorrect.

The final chapter consolidates the entire body of techniques into a coherent framework. Mixed problems resembling those that appear in examination papers are presented with graduated difficulty. Strategies for allocating time, checking work, and choosing between alternative solution methods are discussed explicitly. A comprehensive summary table lists every key definition, theorem, and method introduced across the document, providing a quick reference for last-minute review.

Historical remarks are woven throughout to contextualize the development of the theory. The contributions of Newton, Leibniz, Euler, and other mathematicians are mentioned in passing, not as biographical trivia but as a way of showing how the subject evolved in response to concrete problems. This perspective helps readers appreciate that mathematics is a living discipline shaped by human inquiry rather than a static collection of rules.

The overall tone balances rigor with accessibility. Formal proofs appear where they illuminate the underlying structure of the theory, but technical machinery is kept to the minimum required for genuine understanding. Prerequisites are stated explicitly at the beginning, and a brief glossary of notation is included for readers who may encounter unfamiliar symbols. The document has been designed so that it can be studied independently by a motivated student, used as a supplement to classroom instruction, or referenced selectively by instructors seeking additional material.
